records.name: Parkinsingers Choir
records.summary: A choir for people with Parkinson's, their care partners, and friends. It welcomes singers at every musical level and gives concerts and outreach shows each year.
records.what_you_do: Sing in the choir, perform at the yearly concerts and outreach shows, and take part in the Tango Therapy Project the group lists on its site.

first_step.how: Use the Join the Choir link on parkinsingers.org, or email parkinsingers@gmail.com to ask how to take part
first_step.basis: The site says all musical levels are welcome and has a join link, but the join page did not load during the check

records.notes: IRS legal name: Music Matters International. The site works but shows placeholder text for address and phone and has no dated events, so status is probably_active, not active. Rehearsal times and place are not published on the pages read; ask the group. The community tag disability is used because the choir is built for people with Parkinson's; no exact tag exists.

records.name: NABJ Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the National Association of Black Journalists. It holds membership meetings on the first Wednesday of the month, runs chapter events, and helps fund a scholarship.
records.what_you_do: Go to the monthly membership meeting in person or on Zoom, and take part in chapter events, including the events that honor Black journalists in Philadelphia.

schedule.text: Membership meetings on the first Wednesday of each month, on site and on Zoom

cost.text: Dues not listed on the site

first_step.how: Use the Join Us page at nabj-philadelphia.org/join-us/ to become a member, then RSVP by email for the next first Wednesday meeting
first_step.basis: Meetings are for members, so the join page is the way in, and dues are not listed on the site

records.notes: IRS legal name: Nabj-Philadelphia. The chapter formed in 2023 after the Philadelphia Association of Black Journalists left the national NABJ (see that record). RSVPs go by email through the Contact Us page, which was not read. No phone number is listed. Dues were not found.

records.name: New Jersey Chamber Orchestra
records.summary: A professional nonprofit orchestra based in New Jersey that also plays concerts in Philadelphia, including at the Settlement Music School's Germantown branch. It also does school outreach.
records.what_you_do: Come to a concert, buying a ticket through the site, or give to the orchestra. The site does not describe auditions or other ways to play with the group.

schedule.text: Concerts are listed by date on the website. The latest upcoming one listed was a Saturday evening concert at 8 pm on March 14, 2026.

locations.label: Concert venue: Settlement Music School Germantown Branch

cost.text: Ticket prices not listed on the pages read

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the next concert through the link on njchamberorchestra.org

records.notes: IRS address (805 S Warnock St, Philadelphia) does not appear on the site. The site lists an office at 8 Merion Terrace, Collingswood, NJ, and its Philadelphia link is the concert venue. Published because it performs in Philadelphia. No tag fits a professional orchestra: community_band is the closest tag, and this is a concert-going group, not a community band. Auditions and rehearsals are not described. The most recent past concert listed was January 31, 2026.

records.name: One River Alliance
records.summary: A group that brings neighbors, businesses, and community groups together along the Delaware riverfront. It runs the July 4th FreedomFest fireworks festival.
records.what_you_do: Come out for the July 4th FreedomFest and the events along the river. The site does not describe volunteering or membership.

schedule.text: A yearly July 4th FreedomFest fireworks festival. The 2027 festival is announced for July 2027.

cost.text: No ticket price listed on the site

first_step.how: Plan to attend the July 4th FreedomFest along the Delaware, and check the website for 2027 details as they are posted

records.notes: IRS address is 717 S Columbus Blvd, Unit 1008. The site names an executive director with an email on another company's domain, so no email is recorded. The site says the 2026 festival has already been held; the July 2026 date is inferred from that, not from a page date. The page does not say how to volunteer or join, so publish rests on the public way in (attending the festival). Check before promotion.

records.name: Oral History in the Mid-Atlantic Region (OHMAR)
records.summary: A network that supports people who record life stories as oral historians across the Mid-Atlantic region. It runs workshops and local meetups, holds an annual conference, and gives awards.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a workshop, such as the October 2026 online session on interviewing New Americans, or join a local meetup. Membership and volunteer roles are listed on the site.

schedule.text: Fall workshop on Zoom on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, 6 to 7:30 pm Eastern. Other workshops and meetups are listed on the site.

cost.text: Cost not listed on the workshop page

first_step.how: Register for the October 21, 2026 Zoom workshop through the registration link on ohmar.org
first_step.basis: An open workshop with a public sign-up link; membership details were not read in full

records.notes: IRS address is 315 Chestnut St, Philadelphia, but the site lists no office or local meeting place, so Philadelphia ties are not confirmed. Published because it serves the Mid-Atlantic region, which includes Philadelphia, and its workshops are online. Facebook and Instagram handle is @OHMidAtlantic. The site has no email or phone; its Contact Us page was not read. Awards named on the site (Martha Ross Memorial Prize, Pogue Award) were not read in detail.

records.name: P&P Foundation
records.summary: Promotes journalism in the Philadelphia area. It runs the yearly Philly News Awards, events with local newsmakers, training sessions for reporters and editors, and a mentorship program for student and early-career journalists.
records.what_you_do: Ask about the mentorship program if you are a student or an early-career journalist, and watch for the events and the awards.

locations.label: Pen & Pencil Club building, where the foundation operates

first_step.how: Email ThePandPFoundation@gmail.com and ask how the mentorship program takes people and when the next event is
first_step.basis: Programs are described, but the site does not say who can join or how

records.notes: IRS legal name: P&P Foundation. The site lists no dated events or news. Its only date is a 2025 copyright footer, which is not evidence, so status is probably_active. It is not clear whether this is a grantmaking body or a program nonprofit. It describes its own public programs, so it is published, but please check it against the out of scope rule for private foundations.

locations.label: Chapter office address on the website

cost.text: Dues not listed on the site

first_step.basis: Membership is the main way in and dues are not listed; an email list is available first

records.notes: IRS legal name: Pennsylvania Chapter of Women in Public Finance Inc. The chapter's email is hidden on the page, so only the website and street address are recorded. The award nomination deadline was October 2, 2026, and has passed. No phone number is listed.

cost.text: Dues not listed on the site

first_step.basis: Membership is the main way in and dues are not listed; social events need an RSVP
